chunks: Ali, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Allah, Might and Majestic, Revealed unto Musa (peace be upon him): 'What prevents you from whispering to Me?' So he said: 'O Lord! I delay from the whispering due to the smell of the mouth of a fasting one.' So Allah, Might and Majestic, Revealed unto him: 'O Musa! The smell of the mouth of a fasting one is more aromatic in My Presence than the smell of musk.'

key_terms.خُلُوفُ فَمِ الصَّائِمِ: The smell/odor of the mouth of a fasting person
key_terms.مُنَاجَاة: Intimate conversation or whispering with God

ai.seo_question: Why is the smell of a fasting person's mouth considered better than musk in Islam?
ai.summary: In this well-known hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Prophet Musa (peace be upon him) attributes his hesitation in divine conversation (*munajat*) to the physical odor of fasting, reflecting the human concern for physical purity in spiritual communion. Allah reveals that the natural scent of the fasting believer is more pleasing to Him than musk, a concept (*khaluf al-fam*) that Shia scholars cite as evidence for the spiritual elevation of the body during worship. This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on the holistic nature of fasting, where physical acts of devotion are intrinsically linked to divine pleasure.
